idiom_name: hand-written marker substitution with stdio formatting (strstr + fputs/snprintf)
implementation_notes: C has no template syntax and no standard engine, so the classic structure is written by hand: load the template text, scan for one marker delimiter, fputs the literal spans and snprintf the substituted values into a buffer or FILE stream. The classic form is not merely justified here, it is the realization; keep the marker parser tiny (one delimiter pair), centralise escaping of substituted text in a single helper, and never pass model data as the format string. Library engines (Mustache implementations in C) exist but none is dominant, so adopting one is a build-dependency decision rather than the language's default.
pitfalls: Never pass model data as the printf format string: a value containing %n or %s is a format-string vulnerability, so write fprintf(out, "%s", value) or fputs.
Fixed-size buffers truncate a page silently; snprintf's return value reports what would have been written, so use it to size the buffer or to detect overflow.
Escaping must happen at substitution time and in one place: a single forgotten helper leaks markup/script injection into otherwise correct output.
